tools.description: Chats with project, device, harness/model, sidebar status, and last activity. Status is working, awaitingInput (needs input), completed (unseen result), errored, or idle. statusStale marks expired live reports; terminalActivity explains OSC 7501 reports. sessionStatus is native execution state. Newest activity first.

tools.description: Create a standalone session with kind chat, or a child with kind side. Omitted kind defaults to side with an origin/parent, standalone otherwise. Any connected provider works (see list_harnesses), whichever provider you run on. Delegation is one level deep: a chat that has a parent cannot create chats. With cloud, the chat runs on a Cloud machine of its own (Codex or Claude Code), from a Cloud chat or a project with a GitHub repository. Select a project and/or device; catalogs are validated on that host. Optionally send a first prompt and wait for the reply. For parallel delegation use create_chats, or launch with wait=false and wait only after all chats have started.

access.description: What the agent may do without asking: supervised asks before commands and file changes, auto-accept-edits applies edits and asks before the rest, full-access asks nothing. Questions go to the person in the chat. Must be one of the harness's accessModes (list_harnesses). Defaults to, and can't exceed, the access of the chat you are speaking from.

branch.description: Branch label to record on the chat.

cloud.description: Run on a Cloud machine of its own (cloning the project's GitHub repository) instead of the project's device. From a Cloud chat, the child clones the same repository; without cloud it shares this machine.

Messages are attributed to your chat. mode 'auto' starts a turn when the chat is idle, steers a running turn through its live mailbox (at the next supported input boundary without interrupting the agent). Use mode 'queue' only to explicitly hold a message for later. With wait=true, blocks until the turn finishes and returns the assistant's reply. For parallel work use send_messages, or send to all chats with wait=false before waiting.

tools.description:
Show an interactive visual (chart, table, dashboard, diagram, simulation, 3D view) inline in this chat, above your final text reply; call it before writing that reply. Use it when a visual says more than prose. The reader already sees it, so the reply should not announce, locate, or restate it: add only what the visual doesn't say. To show an image file as it is (a screenshot, a photo), use show_image instead.

A visual is a Luau script (Lua 5.1 plus `+=`, `continue`, and `if` expressions). Zeron runs it in a sandbox (no I/O or network; math.random is seeded, so data is the same on every render) and renders what it returns with Zeron's own native interface. Build data and state at the top level, then return a view function. Zeron calls the view again after every handler, so handlers just assign to state:

local s = ui.state { metric = "p95" }
local data = { { region = "us-east", p95 = 182, p99 = 240 }, { region = "eu-west", p95 = 140, p99 = 210 } }
return function()
return ui.column { gap = 16,
ui.text { "Latency by region", size = "lg", weight = 600 },
ui.tabs { options = { "p95", "p99" }, value = s.metric, on_change = function(v) s.metric = v end },
ui.chart { type = "bar", height = 220, unit = "ms",
x = ui.map(data, function(d) return d.region end),
series = { { name = s.metric, values = ui.map(data, function(d) return d[s.metric] end) } } },
}
end

Zeron runs the script before showing it (setup, render, every draw, and each tab, toggle, slider, and button once) and returns the first error with its line; fix it and call again.

Nodes are props tables: children are the array part, strings are plain text, nil and false children are skipped, and lists of nodes flatten (so ui.map results can be children). Unknown props are errors.
- ui.column { gap = 8, align = "start|center|end", ... }, ui.row { gap = 12, align, justify = "start|center|end|between", wrap = true, ... }, ui.grid { columns = 3, gap = 16, ... }. Any node takes width = px or grow = true inside a row (sliders, charts, tables, canvases, and scenes fill a row's spare width by default), and key = "name" to keep its hover or camera when the tree changes shape. A row or column with on_click = function() end is clickable; hover = true gives it the hover wash.
- ui.text { "plain ", ui.span { "bold", weight = 600, color = "accent", mono = true }, size = "xs|sm|body|lg|xl|2xl", weight = 400-700, color, mono, italic, align, truncate }, or ui.text "string".
- ui.stat { value = "182 ms", label = "p95 latency", delta = "-12%", tone = "success" }: a headline figure over a muted label; tone colors the delta.
- ui.table { columns = { "Region", { label = "p95", align = "end" } }, rows = { { "us-east", 182 }, ... } }: laid out like a markdown table (bold header, hairline row rules), numbers right-aligned; cells are strings, numbers, or nodes.
- ui.chart { type = "bar|line|area|scatter", height = 220, x = { labels }, series = { { name, values = { ... }, color } }, stacked, horizontal (bar), min, max, unit = "ms", prefix = "$", decimals, legend }. Scatter series take points = { { x, y }, ... } (x_unit, x_decimals). Axes, gridlines, the legend, and a hover readout are built in.
- ui.rule {} is a hairline divider; ui.space { size = 16 }; ui.link { label, url = "https://..." } opens like a chat link.
- Controls: ui.tabs { options = { ... }, value, on_change = function(option) end }, ui.toggle { label, value = bool, on_change = function(on) end }, ui.slider { label, value, min, max, step, unit, on_change = function(n) end }, ui.button { label, on_click = function() end, primary = bool }.
- ui.canvas { height = 240, draw = function(g, w, h, t) ... end, animate = bool, on_click = function(x, y) end }: 2D drawing in pixels, origin top-left, w = the reply column's width. g:line(x1, y1, x2, y2, { color, width, dash }), g:polyline(pts, { color, width }), g:polygon(pts, { fill, stroke, width }), g:rect(x, y, w, h, { fill, stroke, radius }), g:circle(x, y, r, { fill, stroke }), g:arc(x, y, r, a0, a1, { color } or { fill, inner = radius } for pie and donut sectors; radians clockwise from 3 o'clock), g:text(x, y, str, { size, color, weight, align = "start|center|end", baseline = "top|middle|bottom", mono }). pts are { x1, y1, x2, y2, ... } or { { x, y }, ... }. g.pointer is { x, y, down } while the pointer is over the canvas (draw hover effects with it); t is seconds, and animate = true redraws every frame while visible.
- ui.scene { height = 320, draw = function(s, t) ... end, orbit = true, spin = 0.3 (turntable radians per second), camera = { yaw = 0.6, pitch = 0.45, zoom = 1 }, animate = bool }: real 3D, y up, rendered on the GPU with depth, soft shadows from a key light, and bloom. Zeron frames the camera on your geometry and the reader drags to orbit. Solids (box, sphere, cylinder, surface, mesh) take material props: roughness (0 mirror to 1 matte), metal (0-1), glow (emits its color and blooms; use for lamps, beams, highlights), glass = true (refracts what's behind it; ior = 1.5, dispersion = 0-1 splits it into a rainbow, as a prism does). Build real forms from several primitives (legs, tops, rims), not single boxes, and give materials so surfaces read as wood, metal, or glass. s:box { at = { x, y, z }, size = { w, h, d } or n, color }, s:sphere { at, radius, color }, s:cylinder { at (base center), radius, height, color }, s:surface { x = { min, max }, z = { min, max }, f = function(x, z) return y end or values = { { ... } }, detail = 32, colors = { "chart1", "chart3" } (a ramp by height), wire = bool }, s:mesh { vertices = { { x, y, z }, ... }, faces = { { 1, 2, 3 }, ... }, color }, s:line(a, b, { color, width }), s:path(points, { color, width }), s:point(at, { radius, color, hint = "shown on hover" }), s:label(at, text, { color, size }), s:grid { size = 10, step = 1 }, s:axes { size = 1, labels = { "x", "y", "z" } }. Physical colors may be "#rrggbb" in scenes (a material's own color: gold, glass, wood), and only there.
- Assets: pass real files in show_visual's assets (name -> path) and scripts use them by name. s:model { asset = "prism.glb", at, rotate = { x, y, z } degrees, scale, fit = 2 (center it and size its longest side), color and material props override the model's own } draws a glTF model with its materials and textures. Solids take texture = "wood.jpg" (multiplied by color; mesh takes uvs = { { u, v }, ... } per vertex). s:environment { asset = "studio.hdr", intensity = 1, background = false } lights the scene from an equirectangular image (an HDR is best) that metal and glass reflect and glass bends; background = true also draws it behind the scene. s:sprite { at, size = 48 (pixels), color, glow = 1, asset = "flare.png" } adds a camera-facing light (a flare or glint; a soft round glow without an asset) that blooms. ui.shader takes textures = { "rock.jpg", ... } as iTexture0-iTexture3 (repeating, mipmapped). Find or make assets with your own tools (download, convert KTX2 or EXR to PNG or HDR) before calling.
- ui.shader { height = 360, code = [[ GLSL ]], buffers = { [[ GLSL ]], ... }, inputs = { speed = s.speed }, blend = "alpha|light|opaque", bloom = 0-3, orbit = bool, spin, camera = { yaw, pitch, zoom }, animate = true }: GPU shaders for what geometry can't express: raymarched SDFs and fractals, light and optics (beams, refraction, dispersion), volumes, fluids, particles, generative art. Write each pass as on Shadertoy: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord), with iResolution (vec3: width and height in pixels, then the display's pixel density), iTime, iTimeDelta, iFrame, iMouse (pixels from the bottom-left; xy where the pointer is, zw where it went down while it's held, negative otherwise), iCamera (vec4 yaw, pitch, zoom, 0; orbit = true lets the reader drag it), every inputs name as a float (bind them to state so sliders and toggles drive the shader), iNoise (a tiling 256x256 random RGBA texture), and iChannel0-iChannel3 with iChannelResolution: buffers run first, in order, each into a float texture that every pass reads as iChannel<i> (an earlier buffer's current frame; a buffer's own previous frame), for multi-pass work like blur, trails, accumulation, and simulation. The shader sits on the chat, never in a box: don't paint a background, vignette, or floor color. By default (blend = "light") the output is emitted light: brightness is opacity and black is clear, right for beams, glows, sparks, and light through glass. For solid shaded objects (fractals, SDF bodies) set blend = "alpha" and write alpha 0 where the ray misses. bloom = 0.6-1.5 adds a soft glow around bright light. The width varies with the reader (a phone is about 350px wide, often narrower than the shader is tall): scale the scene by min(iResolution.x, iResolution.y), not one axis, and keep the subject centered with room on both sides, so it fits and stays centered at any aspect. GLSL errors come back with the pass and line number.
- Helpers: ui.scale(d0, d1, r0, r1) returns a mapping function; ui.ticks(lo, hi, n); ui.fmt(n, { unit, prefix, decimals }) groups digits; ui.map(list, function(v, i) end); ui.range(a, b, step); ui.clamp; ui.lerp; ui.series(i) is "chart<i>"; ui.color(token, alpha); ui.mix(a, b, t). print(...) output comes back to you.

Colors are theme tokens, never hex or color names (except scene materials): text; muted (labels, axes, captions); faint (tertiary notes); accent (the one thing to notice); on-accent (text on an accent mark); success, warning, danger (status only); border (hairlines, gridlines); chart1, chart2, chart3, chart4, chart5, chart6 (series, in order; chart1 is the accent). They follow the reader's theme, light or dark, on frosted glass or an opaque surface, so never assume a background color.

Style, enforced: layout nodes have no fill, border, shadow, padding, or font props. A visual is part of the reply, not a widget, so lay content directly on the chat with type, spacing, and alignment: no cards, tiles, boxed panels, banners, or canvas backgrounds. Stats are a row of plain ui.stat figures; a chart is a plain heading, then the chart; separate sections with gap or one ui.rule. Text renders in Zeron's interface font at the reader's text size: body for most text, sm and xs for labels and notes, lg and xl for headings, 2xl for a headline figure. The width is the reply column (about 720px, as narrow as 360px), so lay out fluidly with grow, wrap, and grid, and give charts, canvases, and scenes heights of 160-420px.

assets.description: Files the script uses, by the name it uses them: { "prism.glb": "models/prism.glb", "sky.hdr": "/tmp/sky.hdr" }. Paths are on this machine, relative to your working directory. glTF models (.glb, or .gltf with everything embedded), PNG, JPEG, WebP, and Radiance .hdr images; at most 16 files, 8 MB each, 10 MB together.

script.description: The Luau visual script: setup at the top level, ending with `return function() return ui.column { ... } end`.

tools.name: show_visual

tools.description: Show an image file (a screenshot, a rendered chart or diagram, a photo) inline in this chat, above your final text reply; call it before writing that reply, once per image, in the order they should appear. PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF, at most 10 MB and 4096 pixels on a side. Zeron copies the file into the chat, so it stays visible after the file changes or is deleted. The reader already sees the image, so the reply should not announce or describe it: add only what the image doesn't show.

path.description: The image file on this machine, absolute or relative to your working directory.

tools.name: show_image
